source: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 15 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 15
knowledgePattern: Unfold and compare the feasible surface routes between opposite edges
solution:
A shortest route can be taken across two faces. Before a path first enters a face containing Y, it is on faces containing X. If it switches between those starting faces, take its last crossing of OA and replace the preceding part by a straight segment from X in the final starting face. Once it enters a face containing Y, replace the rest by the straight segment to Y in that face. These replacements cannot lengthen the path.

There are therefore four pairs to compare: a starting face OAB or OAC followed by a terminal face ABC or OBC. Reflection exchanging O and A fixes X, B, C and Y, so they form two equal-length pairs.

Unfold OAB and ABC across AB. Set A=(0,0), B=(12,0), O=(6,63) and C=(6,−63). Then X=(3,33) and, since BY/BC=1/4, Y=(21/2,−33/2).

The squared straight-line length is (15/2)2+(93/2)2=117. The segment crosses AB internally, so the surface route is valid.

Unfolding OAC with ABC across AC instead gives X=(3,33) and Y=(15/2,−93/2) in coordinates A=(0,0),C=(12,0). The squared length is (9/2)2+(153/2)2=189. This segment also crosses the shared edge internally, but is longer.

The minimum is therefore 117=313 metres. Answer C.

hints.title: Flatten the route
hints.body: Unfold two adjacent faces about their common edge. Lengths along the surface are preserved, and a straight segment in the net is the shortest route for that face pair.
hints.recap: A surface route can be studied on a flat net, provided its straight segment stays inside the required faces.
hints.pitfall: A straight line through the solid interior is not an allowed surface route.
hints.pause: Draw a net joining a face containing X to a face containing Y.

recall.reminder: A surface route can be studied on a flat net, provided its straight segment stays inside the required faces.

hints.title: Place the points using exact heights
hints.body: Split an equilateral face into two right triangles to find its height. Then place X and Y using their stated fractions of the edges.
hints.recap: Pythagoras or an exact right-triangle ratio gives the height of an equilateral triangle.
hints.pitfall: The fraction defining Y is measured from B, not from C.
hints.pause: Find the perpendicular coordinate differences between X and Y in the net.

recall.reminder: Pythagoras or an exact right-triangle ratio gives the height of an equilateral triangle.

hints.title: Compare the competing face pairs
hints.body: Consider each face containing X and each face containing Y. Use reflection symmetry to identify equal cases, and check that each proposed straight segment crosses the intended shared edge.
hints.recap: A candidate net gives one route; a shortest-route claim also requires comparing feasible alternatives.
hints.pitfall: The first convenient unfolding need not always be the shortest one.
hints.pause: Compute the competing squared lengths and justify why extra face crossings cannot improve them.

recall.reminder: A candidate net gives one route; a shortest-route claim also requires comparing feasible alternatives.
